text:
mike: FYI -- since ~07:10 UTC apiserver error rate in eu-west1 jumped; seeing repeated etcd leader elections and an avalanche of pod attach failures for GPU nodes. Noticing a lot of ContainerCreating timeouts.
li: Graphs show etcd commit latency spikes right before the 5xxs. p95 commit > 800ms. GPU attach RPC latency hitting 5s+.
anas: Network team rolled a peering change at 07:05 for a firewall rule cleanup. They said it was metadata-only but we should assume it affected controlplane egress. Any conntrack logs?
julia: On the node pool I see lots of SNAT conn reuse warnings: `conntrack: drop, conntrack table full`. Also iptables-nat counters on the NAT instances are high.
mike: apiserver logs excerpt: 
```
E0705 07:11:02.987654 1 wrap.go:45] http2: response body closed
E0705 07:11:03.123987 1 handler.go:214] apiserver error: 502 Bad Gateway
I0705 07:11:03.223100 1 lease.go:132] etcd: leader changed (old=10.2.1.12 new=10.2.1.9)
```
li: Leader changes correlate with bursts of keeper requeues. Controller-manager spikes requeueing attach-controller tasks which hammer etcd and NAT.
anas: Quick mitigation options: 1) add two temporary NAT gateway instances with larger SNAT tables and reroute node egress 2) throttle attach-controller via feature-flag (set to low throughput) 3) increase etcd election timeouts (longer heartbeat) for the short window 4) shift GPU onboarding traffic to us-west1 for a few minutes.
julia: I'm spinning up 2 nat-large eu-west instances now (using existing ami). ETA ~6m. Also applying `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=300000` across the node pool.
mike: I'm in favor of shifting non-critical attach traffic away from eu-west1 to reduce pressure. Can we patch the scheduler tier to prefer gateway-usw1 for new provisioning?
li: Yes, we can add a short-term routing rule in the provisioning service. I'll push a canary to divert 30% of new attaches immediately.
anas: About etcd: bumping election timeout helps reduce flapping but masks underlying networking problems. Let's only do it as a fallback (increase election timeout from 5s -> 15s) if leader flips continue after NAT scale.
julia: Pushed conntrack and NAT instances are registering. NAT backends now showing reduced port reuse.
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1430, severity=P2, owners=[mike, julia], summary="eu-west1 egress oversubscription -> etcd leader elections -> apiserver 5xx -> GPU attach backlog"
mike: Rolling the attach-controller throttle now: `PATCH /internal/flags` body `{"attach_rate": 10}` (canary applied). Also paused non-urgent GPU batch starts.
li: After the diversion and NATs live apiserver p95 down from 2.4s -> 420ms, etcd leader stable for 7m. Attach queue reduced from 140 -> 32.
anas: Long term followups we should file: - provision dedicated NAT capacity per GPU nodepool (not shared) - audit MTU on peering links (found mtu mismatch 1500 vs 9000 on one hop) - isolate etcd control network (separate subnet + QoS) - add prober that detects SNAT port saturation and auto-scale NATs.
julia: Cost note: extra NAT instances add ~0.6% monthly eu-west infra cost if kept permanently; temporary bursts are negligible. Recommend reserved NATs for peak windows.
mike: Also recommend controller-manager tuning: reduce aggressive requeues during leader transitions and add jitter to backoff. I'll draft PR for tuning flags.
li: For immediate closure: monitoring shows 20m of steady state with normal latencies. Will keep 1h watch. If stable, we'll close incident and open a postmortem.
julia: Confirmed leader stable for 18m, attach queue < 20. Closing ops loop in 42m unless new events. Thanks all.
mike: Good job. Postmortem candidate: root cause likely egress oversubscription + MTU mismatch causing retransmits during leader elections.
